title: review: S4a: graph-aware interference — interference.graph_signal reads graphify-out/graph.json links between the two tasks' files, with per-pair freshness and deterministic fallback
spec:
Goal T-0503, brief .orchestrator/adaptive-parallelism-program.md section P2 (graph evidence is an additional signal; availability not mandatory; fall back when absent or stale). Base goal/T-0503 with S1 (interference.py) merged. Work only in your worktree, commit only on your own branch with the task id in the message, run the full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh before reporting; report sha and failures only.
Facts: graphify-out/graph.json (gitignored, built by .claude/skills/memory/scripts/graph.sh update) is networkx node-link JSON: top-level keys built_at_commit, directed, graph, hyperedges, links, multigraph, nodes; nodes carry id, label, source_file, source_location, community; links carry source and target node ids (verify the exact key names in the file, the local copy from 2026-09-17 has 485 nodes). interference.graph_signal(t1, t2, graph) currently returns [].
1. load_graph(root=ROOT) -> {"nodes_by_file": {source_file: [node ids]}, "links": [(source_id, target_id)], "built_at_commit": str|None, "path": str} or None when the file is missing or unparseable (never raises).
2. graph_fresh_for(paths, graph, git=None) -> True|False|None: True when `git diff --name-only <built_at_commit> HEAD -- <paths>` is empty (none of the pair's files changed since the build), False when it is not, None when built_at_commit is unknown to git or missing; the git callable is injectable for tests.
3. graph_signal(t1, t2, graph): files of each task = literal scope paths plus source files matching its file globs against nodes_by_file keys; when graph_fresh_for(files_a + files_b) is not True return ["graph_stale"] (informational, contributes no level); otherwise return one "graph_link:<file_a>-><file_b>" reason per distinct file pair connected by a link in either direction; these reasons are soft, unless rules["graph_hard_links"] (default 0 = never) is positive and the pair has at least that many links, then hard. classify already appends graph reasons; make sure "graph_stale" never changes level or score, and select_wave passes graph through unchanged.
4. Tests tests/test_interference.py: test_load_graph_reads_node_link_json, test_graph_signal_soft_on_cross_file_link, test_graph_absent_falls_back_deterministic, test_graph_stale_for_pair_skips_signal, test_graph_hard_links_threshold. Existing tests stay green.
acceptance: with a fresh graph, two tasks whose scoped files are linked in graph.json classify as soft with a graph_link reason naming both files; a positive graph_hard_links rule turns that into hard at the threshold
with no graph file, an unparseable file or a stale build for the pair's files, classify returns exactly the deterministic result (plus an informational graph_stale reason when stale) and never raises

tests test_load_graph_reads_node_link_json, test_graph_signal_soft_on_cross_file_link, test_graph_absent_falls_back_deterministic, test_graph_stale_for_pair_skips_signal, test_graph_hard_links_threshold pass and the full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

comments.issue: graph_fresh_for runs `git diff --name-only <commit> HEAD --` with no pathspec when the pair's scope is directory-only (files_a|files_b empty), which diffs the whole repo instead of trivially matching. Cosmetic only: with zero files there can be no graph_link anyway, so classify's level/score is unaffected either way, but the informational graph_stale reason can be spuriously attached.
